questions.stem: Thermal radiation is the transfer of energy by:
questions.explanation: Thermal radiation is the transfer of heat energy through infrared electromagnetic waves. Unlike conduction and convection, it does not require a medium.

questions.stem: Which method of heat transfer can work through a vacuum?
questions.explanation: Only radiation can travel through a vacuum. This is how energy from the Sun reaches Earth across the empty space between them.

questions.stem: Which surface is the best emitter and absorber of thermal radiation?
questions.explanation: Matt black surfaces are the best emitters and absorbers of thermal radiation. Dark, rough surfaces absorb and emit radiation much better than light, shiny surfaces.

questions.stem: Which surface is the best reflector of thermal radiation?
questions.explanation: Shiny, light-coloured surfaces are the best reflectors of thermal radiation. This is why survival blankets are shiny -- they reflect body heat back.

questions.stem: As the temperature of an object increases, the rate of thermal radiation emitted:
questions.explanation: Hotter objects emit thermal radiation at a much greater rate. The rate of emission increases rapidly with temperature.

questions.stem: All objects emit thermal radiation. Which statement is correct?

options.text: All objects at any temperature emit and absorb radiation
Only objects hotter than 100 degrees C emit radiation

questions.explanation: All objects emit and absorb thermal radiation at all temperatures. Hotter objects emit more radiation than they absorb, while cooler objects absorb more than they emit.

questions.stem: A vacuum flask reduces heat loss by radiation by using:
questions.explanation: The silvered (shiny) surfaces inside a vacuum flask reflect thermal radiation back, reducing energy loss by radiation. The vacuum between the walls prevents conduction and convection.
